title: delegated-service-token-role-cache-overgrant-and-audit-metadata-loss
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Summary: A production customer reported two symptoms after a user removal event via SSO group sync: (1) an internal service token briefly retained elevated access to a project resource even after the user's groups were changed, and (2) the audit trail lacked 'grant_source' metadata for the transient permission, making post-mortem attribution impossible. Root cause: RoleCache entries created during RBAC v2 role resolution currently persist resolved role IDs without recording provenance (which SSO group or ad-hoc grant produced that role). A background group-sync job mutates group membership and emits an event, but cache entries are not invalidated fast enough (TTL 10m), and service tokens evaluate cached resolved roles rather than triggering fresh resolution. The race between group-sync and token-use resulted in a short window of over-grant. Additionally, when cached resolved roles were used the audit subsystem only logged the access decision (ALLOW/DENY) but not the underlying grant_source for cached grants, so audit logs cannot distinguish transient grants from persisted grants.

Impact: High for affected customers because over-grants can allow cross-project reads/writes during the window and auditors cannot trace the source. We received a customer escalation (Enterprise ACME Health) and an urgent compliance inquiry.

Repro steps (internal):
1) Create user U in SSO with groups G1 (owner-like) and G2 (normal).
2) Create service token T that acts on behalf of U and triggers role resolution on first use; confirm RoleCache entry added (resolved role set R_owner).
3) Trigger group-sync that removes U from G1 and re-evaluates membership server-side.
4) Immediately use token T to call an API bounded by role R_owner; because cache TTL not expired, RBAC returns ALLOW.
5) Inspect audit log: entry exists for access decision but grant_source is empty or 'cache' with no origin metadata.

Immediate mitigation for customers:
- Advice: Revoke service tokens for affected users (manual) and rotate keys.
- Interim platform mitigation: Reduce RoleCache TTL to 30s via feature flag and trigger a manual cache invalidation hook for SSO group-sync events.

Proposed fix:
1) Persist provenance metadata alongside resolved-role entries in RoleCache: include grant_source (SSO_GROUP_SYNC, TEAM_ASSIGN, DIRECT_GRANT), grant_id (group id or grant id), and resolved_at timestamp.
2) When audit subsystem logs an access decision that used a cache entry, include grant_source/grant_id in the audit event so post-hoc investigations can attribute the permission.
3) Wire SSO group-sync event bus to proactively invalidate or mark stale RoleCache entries for affected users and service tokens.
4) Add a cache-eviction audit event when invalidation occurs (cache.evict with reason).
5) Add end-to-end tests and a canary rollout behind rbac_v2_cache_metadata feature flag.

Notes on scope: This touches the RBAC resolution path (backend), role cache serialization, audit pipeline (event schema), and SSO sync hooks. The change must be backward compatible for stored cache blobs (migration path).
acceptance_criteria: RoleCache entries include grant_source and grant_id fields (string) and are serialized safely for the cluster
Audit events for cached decisions include grant_source/grant_id when present
SSO group-sync produces a cache invalidation event that clears affected RoleCache entries within 5s in canary region
Automated tests cover race between group-sync and token use; CI shows no false positives
Feature flag rbac_v2_cache_metadata is default OFF; rollout plan documented
Customer ACME Health confirms rotation guidance and verifies no further incidents after mitigation
tasks: Design: schema for grant_source/grant_id in RoleCache and audit event (Priya to draft)
Backend: add provenance fields to role resolution flow and cache write (Miguel)
SSO: emit user-scoped cache invalidation messages from group-sync job (Liam)
Audit: augment access-decision events to include provenance when available (Sara)
Infra: migration strategy for preexisting cache blobs (write-on-read upgrade), and fallback behavior
E2E: create deterministic test that reproduces race and asserts audit contains grant_source (integration tests)
Docs: runbook update for customer support + KB article for manual revocation steps
Rollout: implement feature flag, deploy to canary, monitor metrics (overgrant_count, cache_hit_rate, audit_missing_provenance)
Postmortem: coordinate customer communication and SOC attestation update

Edge case: nested inheritance (team -> project -> resource) may require an ordered provenance list — suggesting we store primary_grant and an ancestry list of grant_ids as optional. Parking full ancestry for now to reduce risk; primary_grant should cover most audits.
